reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents promotional coverage of a named MEXC futures-trading competition with a stated USDT prize pool, participation rules, trading-volume thresholds, participant limits, rankings, and leverage guidance. The material also describes crypto investment as speculative and potentially loss-making, while related crypto links and a separate CoinFutures advertisement are presented as promotional context without establishing fraud or a deceptive outcome.

citations.quote: MEXC Launches Anniversary Futures Trading Competition With $10 Million USDT Prize Pool!
Get your teams ready, get ready to trade, get ready to profit.
if you want to click the link down in the description below, you've got a great article that basically summarizes everything that you would need to see.
Teams are ranked according to their combined futures profit and loss.
Each day, the top 200 traders by future trading volume receive a share of that day's portion, rewarding steady participation

opening.argument: The video ties a large monetary reward directly to viewer action: viewers are told to form teams, trade futures, and pursue profit, while the event page invites them to register. The early-bird reward likewise requires reaching a specified futures-trading volume. This is not merely a passive announcement; it presents an attractive USDT pool as the reason to enter the platform and perform the required activity. The combination of a reward promise, registration pathway, and trading requirement is a solicitation to obtain a financial benefit through a linked action.

citations.quote: Get your teams ready, get ready to trade, get ready to profit.
the first 1 000 participants who reach 50 000 usdt in futures trading volume also qualify for a separate 20 000 usdt early bird reward pool

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a competition does not remove the solicitation. The supplied material still directs viewers to a description link, asks them to register or join teams, and connects eligibility to futures trading activity. Ranking language describes conditions of the pitch; it does not establish that ordinary viewers can realistically obtain the advertised rewards. The central message remains: take the requested trading action for a chance at substantial USDT rewards.

citations.quote: if you want to click the link down in the description below
Team members are able to join during the registration window from April 12th until May 3rd.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quotes show a promotional competition with explicit eligibility mechanics, not a guaranteed or low-effort payout. “Get ready to profit” is encouragement, while the actual rules require ranking, volume, or team performance. The event page visibly frames the offer as “Trade as a team and share” the pool, so the material does not show that merely clicking or registering produces a reward.

citations.quote: Teams are ranked according to their combined futures profit and loss.
Each day, the top 200 traders by future trading volume receive a share of that day's portion

opening.argument: Several unusually aggressive signals appear together: a ten-million-USDT headline prize, a limited early-bird pool, high-frequency trading encouragement, and leverage presented as a way to reach the threshold quickly. The surrounding descriptions also advertise very high leverage and potential sign-up bonuses. Even where the speaker mentions trading volume, the presentation emphasizes speed, scale, and upside rather than showing that a typical participant will receive anything. That combination makes the reward pitch materially more misleading than a neutral notice about an ordinary promotion.

you could you could literally hit 50 000 usdt in a couple trades uh or a couple hours if you're going out there and trading on leverage

rebuttal.rebuttal: The disclaimer and generic risk language do not neutralize the stronger promotional signals in the actual pitch. The speaker still highlights a huge prize, urges high-frequency activity, and says leverage can reach the qualifying volume in hours. A warning that investments can lose value does not explain the probability of winning, the cost of trading, or how the advertised rewards are distributed among participants.

citations.quote: you could you could literally hit 50 000 usdt in a couple trades uh or a couple hours if you're going out there and trading on leverage
high frequency as well
The value of your investments may go up or down.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals describe risk and competition mechanics rather than deception. The material expressly says the threshold is futures trading volume, not profit, and the event distributes rewards by rankings and daily volume. The separate leverage advertisement in the description is promotional context, but it does not prove that this MEXC competition guarantees an easy return or conceals losses.

This is a high-risk investment and you should not expect to be protected if something goes wrong.

opening.argument: Although presented through an article and market-style explanation, the content functions as a direct acquisition funnel. It repeatedly tells viewers to use links, become a team captain, join a team, register, and trade on the named exchange. The article and screenshots supply promotional proof points such as prize totals, rankings, participant figures, and estimated rewards, then place a visible “Visit MEXC” or “Register Now” pathway beside them. That is promotional steering toward participation, not detached reporting.

citations.quote: if you want to click the link down in the description below
Think of becoming a team captain. You have a link down in the description to set all up.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The article framing is precisely what makes the pitch persuasive: it gives the solicitation an informational appearance while directing viewers to MEXC and emphasizing rewards. The speaker does not merely summarize rules; he says to get teams ready, trade, profit, and use the description link. A disclaimer about entertainment cannot change the functional call to register and trade.

citations.quote: Get your teams ready, get ready to trade, get ready to profit.
make sure to check out you guys get links for that down in the description below

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The presence of calls to action establishes promotion, but promotion alone does not establish a scam. The content identifies the exchange, event rules, dates, ranking criteria, and reward allocation, and it includes explicit speculative-risk language. The quoted links therefore support ordinary advertising or event coverage; they do not show fabricated rewards, hidden conditions, or a deceptive outcome.
